extracted.intended_audience: students, instructors, and readers of Hatcher's 'Algebraic Topology' seeking errata and clarification
extracted.subtask_description: A cumulative errata/clarifications list for the textbook 'Algebraic Topology' (Hatcher), documenting corrections to statements, proofs, exercises, notation, hypotheses, figures, and references across chapters and the appendix. Used by readers to check and correct printed copies and to guide the online version.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and include necessary hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure theorem statements, propositions, examples, and exercises explicitly include all hypotheses needed for the arguments (e.g., assume X is Hausdorff, path-connected, finite-dimensional, connected, or that maps are quotient maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many items add hypotheses: Exercise 21 (assume X Hausdorff); Example 1.21 (assume X_alpha path-connected); Exercise 6 (assume discrete subspace closed); Exercise 27 (require f be a quotient map, not just surjective); add finite-dimensional CW hypothesis in several places; require injectivity of edge homomorphisms in Section 1.B Exercise 9, etc. When a special case (e.g., n=0 or n=1) breaks a general statement, either exclude the trivial case or add the special-case handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct mathematical assertions (statements/labels/signs/indices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix incorrect mathematical claims, labels, signs, indices, and other formula-level mistakes so the stated results are accurate (e.g., change 'homology group' to 'cohomology group', fix minus/equals, change H_n to H_{n+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Chapter 3 intro: 'homology group' -> 'cohomology group'; psi - delta phi: replace minus by equals; change H^n(X,A) to H^n(X,A;G); change H_n(X) to H_{n+1}(X); adjust exponents and signs in various displayed formulas (several explicit line corrections). Verify low-dimensional edge cases (degree for n=0) and add n>0 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and typographical consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistent notation (superscripts vs subscripts, tildes, fonts, blackboard bold, Greek letters) and fix typographical errors that affect meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: replace 0t_i by 0x_i; add tildes over H_n where needed; change Koenig -> König; change 'cover space' -> 'covering space'; change Z to blackboard bold Z; change parentheses, commas, semicolons in cohomology notation; fix misplaced superscripts/subscripts (e.g., n-i vs n-i-1), missing primes, missing bars, add absolute-value bars in examples, fix accented names, and ensure consistent italic fonts for symbols. Small typographical errors that change semantics should be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct cross-references and bibliographic citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix references to theorem/proposition/exercise numbers, example numbers, and bibliographic names so cross-references point to the intended material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many corrections change references: e.g., Corollary 2.15 vs 2.11, Corollary 2B.7 vs Prop 2B.6, Theorem 2.26 vs 2.19, references to exercises moved between chapters, change 4K.1 to 4L.1, correct citation of Adams and Wilkerson and later work (Andersen & Grodal). Check every in-text reference to ensure it matches the current edition/online version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify point-set topology caveats and continuity arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where arguments rely on point-set topology facts (continuity, compact-open issues, union of subspaces), make assumptions explicit (e.g., A closed in X) or add the missing point-set-topology arguments in the Appendix/online text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: homotopy extension property argument requires A closed in X for continuity; discussion about join associativity warns that set-theoretic associativity may fail topologically unless using CW topologies; expand proofs or add Appendix material when the hypothesis is not automatically satisfied. For subtle continuity steps, either add hypotheses or expand the argument in the appendix/online version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and expand proofs where gaps or omissions occur
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proof is incomplete or misses subtle points (e.g., Poincaré duality steps, injectivity/surjectivity claims, sign issues), revise the proof and provide corrected or expanded arguments (often in the online version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: proof of Proposition 3F.12 had a gap (torsion oversight) — corrected in online version; Lemma 4.10 statement and proof revised to give stronger homotopy property; several proofs rewritten for clarity or correctness (Hurewicz theorem, additivity of Sq^i argument). Provide corrected proofs in the online errata or expanded Appendix material as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust or delete incorrect exercises/parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or modify exercise parts that are incorrect or rely on circular reasoning; add missing hypotheses or provide counterexamples where the original statement is false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Section 1.2, Exercise 5 part (b) is simply wrong and should be omitted; Section 2.2, Exercise 34 deleted due to circular reasoning; Exercise revisions to include missing assumptions or to relocate problems to a more appropriate section. When an exercise is incorrect, either supply the corrected statement or remove it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify basepoint and path conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit choices and conventions about basepoints, path orientations, and relative fundamental group notations to avoid abuse of notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: note reduced suspension depends on basepoint choice; relative pi_1 coset conventions clarified (use H alpha vs alpha H), change pi_0(A,x_0) to i_*(pi_0(A,x_0)), discuss basepoint issues in proofs and lemmas. Where path-direction conventions affect group labels, state the convention explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagram and figure corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix diagrams and figures: arrow directions, commutativity up to sign, missing labels, and small diagram typos that affect the asserted relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vertical arrows pointing the wrong way on a diagram (fixed in later printing); large diagram commuting only up to sign unless generators chosen; missing dot for composition between g_1 and igures; small diagrams replaced by larger corrected diagrams in later printings. Ensure diagrams truly represent the algebraic/topological assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficient-group and local-vs-ordinary coefficient corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct the use of coefficient groups in cohomology/homology statements (e.g., change H^n(X,A) to include coefficient group, fix local coefficient vs ordinary coefficient statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: change H^n(X,A) to H^n(X,A;G); in Poincar�e9 duality with local coefficients adjust occurrences of M_R to R or vice versa as appropriate; ensure notation uses semicolons/commas correctly in cohomology groups; clarify when local coefficients are intended and correct proofs accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle low-dimensional and special-case exceptions carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly treat low-dimensional (n=0, n=1) or degenerate cases where general statements fail or require different notation (e.g., reduced homology, empty boundaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: notion of degree not interesting at n=0 so exclude or treat separately; Example 2.23: special-case n=1 needs modification since boundary of D^{n-1} is empty and pair is not 'good'; add n>0 conditions in several places. For each theorem/example, check boundary cases and state exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign, grading and graded-commutativity care in algebraic manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: When manipulating graded tensor products, Hopf algebras, Steenrod operations, etc., include the required sign/interchange conventions and grading conditions to avoid missing sign changes or omitted factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: definition of coproduct in tensor product of Hopf algebras neglected interchange of middle factors (graded sign); several proofs have sign problems (e.g., Lemma 4L.14); reverse signs on exponents in displayed formulas. Wherever graded commutativity is used, state the sign rule and check permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and literature updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Update historical comments and references to reflect corrected statements about prior results and to cite the correct or most recent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Frobenius theorem needs identity hypothesis; Hurwitz's result clarified; Adams & Wilkerson reference corrected to Andersen & Grodal for the completed proof; add references (Gubeladze) where algebraic problems were solved. When historical assertions are made, verify and, if necessary, correct or refine them with proper citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index and table-of-contents corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix index entries, page numbers, and table of contents page numbers to point readers to the correct locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: add page for cup product definition (206), correct Hurewicz Theorem index pages (366 and 371), projective space quaternion reference page. Also correct TOC item 'Applications to Cell Complexes' page number. Update indices when content shifts in revised printings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note which corrections have been incorporated online or in later printings
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if a correction has already been incorporated into later printings or the online version and provide pointers to the pdf errata or online corrected text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many entries state 'The online version of the book gives a corrected version' or 'This has been revised in later printings'. Keep a pdf errata and online version link for corrected proofs, extended explanations, and items that required larger rewrites (e.g., expanded Appendix sections, revised proofs and charts).
